$comment: REAL GATE for the EP packaging script — `pnpm typecheck:pack-ep`, chained
into `pnpm typecheck` and therefore into CI via .github/workflows/ci.yml.
Why a dedicated program instead of a `// @ts-check` pragma in pack-ep.mjs:
a config entry is a thing the compiler resolves, so a renamed or deleted
file becomes TS6053 and turns the gate red. A source pragma just stops
being checked the moment someone edits the line above it.
Relationship to the other two scripts programs — none of them can mask
another, because each covers a different set of files:
- tsconfig.scripts.json         include scripts/__tests__, checkJs:false.
It checks the .ts tests against the signatures pack-ep.mjs INFERs, so a
.mjs type change that breaks a test call site fails there. It does not
check the .mjs bodies at all.
- this file                     files: the two packaging scripts,
checkJs:true. It checks the .mjs bodies. It contains no tests, so it
cannot report a broken test call site.
- tsconfig.scripts-checkjs.json include scripts, checkJs:true. Backlog
only — NOT wired into `pnpm typecheck` and referenced by no CI workflow,
so it can neither enforce nor hide anything in the two above.
sign-ep.mjs is listed explicitly even though tsc pulls it in anyway as a
hard import of pack-ep.mjs: naming it means the gate's stated scope is
exactly what it checks, and dropping the import cannot silently shrink it.
No compiler option is relaxed here. checkJs is on; strict,
noImplicitAny, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters and skipLibCheck all
inherit from tsconfig.json unchanged.
